description: Byte-wise zero test of a u32 (four masked compares) not folded to (x - 0x01010101) & ~x & 0x80808080
notes: Found while screening C candidates: the better version is the classic one from Bit Twiddling Hacks ('Determine if a word has a zero byte', also Hacker's Delight 6-1). Naive test of the four bytes written by us. clang trunk -O3 -march=skylake vectorizes it into a <4 x i32> and, icmp, bitcast and icmp: 7 IR instructions. expected.ll is the subtract/and-not/and test: 6 IR instructions. No LLVM issue found for this idiom. Gain estimated by llvm-mca (godbolt llc and llvm-mca trunk, -mcpu=skylake, cycles per 100 iterations): 255 vs 169. expected.ll proven correct (refinement) by Alive2 alive-tv, 2026-10-28: src = clang trunk -O3 IR of src.c (godbolt cclang_trunk, -O3 --target=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -march=skylake -emit-llvm -S -g0) renamed @src, tgt = expected.ll renamed @tgt, identical signature; output 'Transformation seems to be correct!' with no warning. Run on Alive2's own Compiler Explorer instance (alive2.llvm.org/ce, compiler id 'alive'), since godbolt.org does not host alive-tv.
